title: fix(gateway): hide host disk paths from read-only system info
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: read-only Gateway callers can see host filesystem paths in `system.info`, including the state directory.

## User Impact

Read-only callers retain state-volume capacity totals but no longer receive `diskPath` or `disks`. Admin callers keep mounted-disk details and the state-directory fallback. Read-only Control UI connections consequently show no per-disk meters. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The RPC uses the existing admin-scope check to decide whether to collect and return paths, matching the connection snapshot's state-directory policy. It skips mounted-disk discovery for non-admin callers and keeps the existing capacity sampler. No new state, cache, or policy owner is introduced; the added code covers the scoped response and its regression test.

## Evidence

Head: `2229f7b346fbf0492c100f46592de9408107d5c4`.

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/system-info.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/system-info.authority.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 9/9 passed; Vitest wall time 36.53s, including 16.26s for the authenticated Gateway case. CI timing is not yet available. The new network regression failed on the base because a read-only response exposed the state-directory path.
- An isolated loopback Gateway with synthetic signed, paired-device credentials exercised real WebSocket authentication, the production RPC handler, and native Linux disk sampling. Read-only responses omit path fields before and after an admin warms the shared disk snapshots, while preserving total/free bytes. Admin responses retain paths and mounted disks.
- A separate admin device starts `system.info`; disk I/O pauses after native sampling, its token is revoked through the public admin RPC, then the read resumes. The request fails with authorization close code 4001 and active work drains; no successful path-bearing response reaches that client. An unaffected admin can still read paths afterward. Only the I/O pause is instrumented; authentication, revocation, dispatch, and response guards stay real.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json`, focused oxlint with `--openclaw-focused-config`, oxfmt, the staged test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` and checks for every changed TypeScript file also passed on this head.
- The separate 183-line test allocation covers this patch's handler regression, admin fixture adjustments, and network-boundary proof. The latter protects authenticated/cache/revocation behavior that a direct-handler test cannot prove.

Environment: local Linux, isolated state and claimed loopback port, synthetic credentials, no external provider calls. No macOS host or browser session was exercised. Native discovery remains unchanged. Local ClawSweeper completed at this exact head: overall B (Platinum), patch B, proof B, sufficient terminal evidence, cleared security, and no code findings or Before merge risks. The accepted result and behavior-proof comment are published on this PR.

Regression risk: clients that relied on filesystem paths without admin scope lose those fields and per-disk UI meters. Admin responses retain their existing shape; capacity totals remain readable.

<details>
<summary>Exact-head runtime capture</summary>

Captured local terminal result (Linux; synthetic credentials and isolated state):

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
2229f7b346fbf0492c100f46592de9408107d5c4
$ pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/system-info.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/system-info.authority.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/system-info.authority.integration.test.ts > withholds disk paths on authenticated reads and suppresses a revoked in-flight response 16263ms
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  9 passed (9)
Duration  36.53s (tests 48%, transform 39%, import 11%, worker 1%, setup 1%)
Exit status: 0
```

The negative control ran the same network regression with the parent production implementation: exit 1 at the first read-only response (`diskPath` was present, expected undefined). The fixed run above uses the committed test and final production source. The only controlled I/O pause is in the committed test; response values, auth checks, and token revocation are not mocked. The successful test reaches both read-only responses, the path-bearing admin response, revocation during the paused read, the 4001 close, the drained-work check, and a subsequent unaffected admin read.

</details>
